passages.text: Now about the times and seasons, brothers, we do not need to write to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul speaks about the times and seasons.
Paul says he does not need to write to them about these things.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν χρόνων καὶ τῶν καιρῶν ἀδελφοί οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ὑμῖν γράφεσθαι

passages.text: For you are fully aware that the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
passages.sermon:
You are fully aware of this truth.
The Day of the Lord will come.
It will come suddenly.
It will come like a thief in the night.
passages.original: αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκριβῶς οἴδατε ὅτι ἡμέρα Κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης ἐν νυκτὶ οὕτως ἔρχεται

passages.text: While people are saying, “Peace and security,” destruction will come upon them suddenly, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
passages.sermon:
Some people will say, "Peace and security." 
Destruction will come to them suddenly. 
This destruction will come like labor pains come to a pregnant woman. 
They will not escape.
passages.original: ὅταν λέγωσιν Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια τότε αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐφίσταται ὄλεθρος ὥσπερ ἡ ὠδὶν τῇ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσῃ καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκφύγωσιν

passages.text: But you, brothers, are not in the darkness so that this day should overtake you like a thief.
passages.sermon:
You are brothers in Christ.
You do not live in darkness.
The Day of the Lord will not surprise you like a thief.
You are prepared for that day.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀδελφοί οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σκότει ἵνα ἡ ἡμέρα ὑμᾶς ὡς κλέπτης καταλάβῃ

passages.text: For you are all sons of the light and sons of the day; we do not belong to the night or to the darkness.
passages.sermon:
You are all sons of the light.
You are all sons of the day.
We do not belong to the night.
We do not belong to the darkness.
passages.original: πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς υἱοὶ φωτός ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ἡμέρας Οὐκ ἐσμὲν νυκτὸς οὐδὲ σκότους

passages.text: So then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us remain awake and sober.
passages.sermon:
You are brothers in Christ.
You are not in darkness.
You are sons of light and sons of the day.
You do not belong to the night or to darkness.
So do not sleep like the others.
Stay awake.
Be sober.
passages.original: ἄρα οὖν μὴ καθεύδωμεν ὡς οἱ λοιποί ἀλλὰ γρηγορῶμεν καὶ νήφωμεν

passages.text: For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
passages.sermon: People who sleep, sleep at night.\r\nPeople who get drunk, get drunk at night.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ καθεύδοντες νυκτὸς καθεύδουσιν καὶ οἱ μεθυσκόμενοι νυκτὸς μεθύουσιν

passages.text: But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
passages.sermon:
We belong to the day.
We must stay sober.
We must put on faith and love like a breastplate.
We must put on hope of salvation like a helmet.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἡμέρας ὄντες νήφωμεν ἐνδυσάμενοι θώρακα πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ περικεφαλαίαν ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας

passages.text: For God has not appointed us to suffer wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon: God did not appoint us to suffer wrath.\r\nGod appointed us to obtain salvation.\r\nWe receive salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὅτι οὐκ ἔθετο ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εἰς ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ εἰς περιποίησιν σωτηρίας διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: He died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ died for us.
He died for our sake.
He did this so we may live together with Him.
We may be awake.
We may be asleep.
No matter our state, we may live with Him.
passages.original: τοῦ ἀποθανόντος περὶ ἡμῶν ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν εἴτε καθεύδωμεν ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν

passages.text: Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
He tells them to encourage each other.
He tells them to build each other up.
They are already doing this.
He wants them to continue.
passages.original: Διὸ παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε εἷς τὸν ἕνα καθὼς καὶ ποιεῖτε

passages.text: But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters.
He asks them to recognize certain people in their community.
These people work hard among the believers.
They lead the church in the Lord.
They give instruction to the believers.
passages.original: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί εἰδέναι τοὺς κοπιῶντας ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ προϊσταμένους ὑμῶν ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ νουθετοῦντας ὑμᾶς

passages.text: In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters in the church.
He tells them to honor their leaders.
These leaders work hard among them.
They guide the church in the Lord.
They teach and instruct the people.
Paul says to hold these leaders in the highest regard.
He says to do this with love.
He says to respect them because of their work.
Paul also tells everyone to live in peace with each other.
passages.original: καὶ ἡγεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ διὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτῶν εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς

passages.text: And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters.
He urges them to act.
He tells them to warn those who are unruly.
He tells them to encourage those who are fainthearted.
He tells them to help those who are weak.
He tells them to be patient with everyone.
passages.original: Παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί νουθετεῖτε τοὺς ἀτάκτους παραμυθεῖσθε τοὺς ὀλιγοψύχους ἀντέχεσθε τῶν ἀσθενῶν μακροθυμεῖτε πρὸς πάντας

passages.text: Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters in the church.
He gives them instructions for how to live.
Do not repay evil with evil.
Do not let anyone return wrong for wrong.
Always do what is good.
Pursue good for each other.
Pursue good for everyone.
passages.original: Ὁρᾶτε μή τις κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ τινι ἀποδῷ ἀλλὰ πάντοτε τὸ ἀγαθὸν διώκετε καὶ εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας

passages.text: Rejoice at all times.
passages.sermon: Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters in Thessalonica.\r\nHe tells them to rejoice.\r\nHe says to rejoice at all times.
passages.original: Πάντοτε χαίρετε

passages.text: Pray without ceasing.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Christians in Thessalonica.
He told them to pray.
He told them to pray at all times.
He told them to never stop praying.
passages.original: ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε

passages.text: Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon: God wants you to give thanks in every circumstance.\r\nGod’s will for you is in Christ Jesus.\r\nYou should always be thankful.
passages.original: ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε τοῦτο γὰρ θέλημα Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Do not extinguish the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit comes from God.
The Holy Spirit works in believers.
Do not put out the Holy Spirit’s fire.
Do not stop the Holy Spirit’s work.
passages.original: Τὸ Πνεῦμα μὴ σβέννυτε

passages.text: Do not treat prophecies with contempt, but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.
passages.sermon: Do not treat prophecies with contempt.\r\nTest all things.\r\nHold fast to what is good.
passages.original: προφητείας μὴ ἐξουθενεῖτε πάντα δὲ δοκιμάζετε τὸ καλὸν κατέχετε

passages.text: Abstain from every form of evil.
passages.sermon:
God calls you to live in holiness.
God wants you to avoid sin.
Stay away from every kind of evil.
Do not take part in anything that is wrong.
passages.original: ἀπὸ παντὸς εἴδους πονηροῦ ἀπέχεσθε

passages.text: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of peace.
God Himself can make you holy.
God can make you holy in every way.
God can keep your spirit holy.
God can keep your soul holy.
God can keep your body holy.
God can keep you blameless.
God can keep you blameless until our Lord Jesus Christ comes.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς ὁλοτελεῖς καὶ ὁλόκληρον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ τὸ σῶμα ἀμέμπτως ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τηρηθείη

passages.text: The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
passages.sermon: God calls you.\r\nGod is faithful.\r\nGod will do what He promises.
passages.original: πιστὸς ὁ καλῶν ὑμᾶς ὃς καὶ ποιήσει

passages.text: Brothers, pray for us as well.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
He calls them brothers.
He asks them to pray.
He asks them to pray for him and his companions.
passages.original: Ἀδελφοί προσεύχεσθε καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church.
He speaks to believers in Jesus Christ.
He calls them brothers.
He tells them to greet all the brothers.
He says to use a holy kiss for this greeting.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς πάντας ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ

passages.text: I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church.
\r\nPaul speaks with authority from the Lord.
\r\nPaul gives a command.
\r\nPaul commands the believers.
\r\nPaul says, "Read this letter to all the brothers."
\r\nPaul wants every brother to hear this letter.
\r\nPaul makes this command before the Lord.
passages.original: Ἐνορκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Κύριον ἀναγνωσθῆναι τὴν ἐπιστολὴν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς

passages.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
passages.sermon: Jesus Christ is our Lord.\r\nJesus Christ gives grace.\r\nMay the grace of Jesus Christ be with you.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν
